# Relay protocol reference

Schema version: `52` · Native methods: `168` · MCP tools: `152`

| Native method | MCP tool | Parameters | Access | Description |

| `runtime.status` | `runtime_status` | — | read-only | Read the current editor or game mode, pause, frame, simulation time and resolution state. |
| `runtime.play` | `runtime_play` | — | mutating | Start a temporary game session from the authored scene. Stop restores the authored scene and discards runtime changes. |
| `runtime.stop` | `runtime_stop` | — | mutating | Stop the current game session and restore the authored scene without changing undo history. |
| `runtime.pause` | `runtime_pause` | — | mutating | Pause a running game so its scene can be inspected deterministically. |
| `runtime.resume` | `runtime_resume` | — | mutating | Resume a paused game after inspection or a controlled frame step. |
| `runtime.step` | `runtime_step` | `frames`: integer = `1` | mutating | Advance an exact number of deterministic game frames, including while paused. |
| `runtime.quit` | `runtime_shutdown` | — | mutating | Request an orderly shutdown of the runtime owned by this MCP bridge. |
| `editor.camera.status` | `editor_camera_status` | — | read-only | Read the live editor inspection viewpoint used by Vulkan captures. Unavailable without an editor. Does not modify scene cameras. |
| `editor.camera.set` | `editor_camera_set` | `target_x`: number<br>`target_y`: number<br>`target_z`: number<br>`yaw`: number<br>`pitch`: number<br>`distance`: number<br>`mode`: string = `"inspector"` | mutating | Set the live inspector camera target, orbit angles in radians and distance for visual confirmation using render_capture source vulkan. View-only: no scene or undo changes. |
| `editor.camera.frame` | `editor_camera_frame` | `entity`: string (required) | mutating | Frame an entity and its descendant bounds in the live inspection view before Vulkan capture. Does not change selection, scene cameras or undo history. |
| `render.capture` | `render_capture` | `filename`: string = `"agent-capture.png"`<br>`source`: string = `"vulkan"` | mutating | Save the current rendered frame in Relay's captures directory for visual inspection. |
| `render.capture_async` | `render_capture_async` | `filename`: string = `"agent-async.png"`<br>`source`: string | mutating | Capture real Vulkan or deterministic CPU frames through bounded background image workers. |
| `render.capture_cancel` | `render_capture_cancel` | `job`: integer (required) | mutating | Cancel a queued image or GPU readback job; writing and completed jobs cannot be cancelled. GPU slots remain alive until their fence completes. |
| `render.capture_status` | `render_capture_status` | `job`: integer (required) | read-only | Check whether an asynchronous capture is queued, writing, complete or failed. |
| `render.capabilities` | `render_capabilities` | — | read-only | Create a temporary Vulkan device and report adapter and modern rendering support. |
| `render.graph` | `render_graph` | — | read-only | Read compiled render passes, resources, dependencies and access transitions. |

| `render.upload_status` | `render_upload_status` | — | read-only | Read Vulkan asset upload budgets, staging peaks, estimated resident bytes and transfer-path state. |
| `render.assets` | `render_assets` | — | read-only | List built-in and imported meshes, materials and textures currently available to scene renderer components. |
| `assets.formats` | `asset_import_formats` | — | read-only | Report model formats and feature coverage available in this Relay build, including Godot-compatible interchange paths. |
| `assets.import_model` | `asset_import_model` | `filename`: string (required)<br>`instantiate`: boolean = `true`<br>`preset`: string = `"scene"` | mutating | Import a model from the project-local assets directory using a content-addressed identity and optionally instantiate its node hierarchy. |
| `assets.browse` | `asset_browse` | `directory`: string = `""` | read-only | List the folders and files in one project folder, folders first, with each entry's asset kind. Hidden entries, symlinks and .relayproject files are omitted; importable models are marked. |
| `assets.search` | `asset_search` | `query`: string = `""`<br>`folder`: string = `""`<br>`paths`: boolean = `false`<br>`kinds`: string_array | read-only | Find project files and folders below the project root (or one folder) whose names contain every word of the query, optionally limited to asset kinds. Hidden entries, symlinks and .relayproject files are skipped; at most 512 results. |
| `assets.create_folder` | `asset_create_folder` | `path`: string (required) | mutating | Create a new, empty folder inside an existing project folder. |
| `assets.move` | `asset_move` | `from`: string (required)<br>`to`: string (required) | mutating | Rename or move a project file or folder without overwriting. Import records follow moved models; project scene files and the project file cannot move. |
| `assets.delete` | `asset_delete` | `path`: string (required) | mutating, destructive | Move a project file or folder into the hidden .relay-trash folder, where it can be recovered by hand. Project scene files and the project file cannot be deleted. |
| `shaders.read` | `shaders_read` | `path`: string (required) | read-only | Read a Relay shader (.relay-shader): its text, type, render modes, uniforms (with types, hints, ranges and defaults), and compile errors by line. A shader being previewed also returns the preview text. See docs/shaders.md for the language: shader_type surface or post_process, uniform declarations, and void vertex()/fragment() functions writing built-ins such as ALBEDO, ROUGHNESS, VERTEX or COLOR. |
| `shaders.write` | `shaders_write` | `path`: string (required)<br>`text`: string<br>`create`: boolean = `false`<br>`type`: string = `"surface"`<br>`effect`: string | mutating, destructive | Create or replace a Relay shader file and compile it, returning its compile errors by line. Materials using it redraw at once. With create and no text, starts from the template for type, or from one of Relay's ready-made post-processing effects (effect: bloom, color_grading or vignette), which then belongs to the project like any other shader. Clears any preview of the file. |
| `shaders.preview` | `shaders_preview` | `path`: string (required)<br>`text`: string | mutating | Compile shader text without saving it and draw every material using the shader with it, so edits show in the viewport before they are saved. Omit text to stop previewing and use the file again. Returns compile errors by line. |
| `assets.material` | `asset_material` | `path`: string (required) | read-only | Read a surface or post-processing material (.relay-material): its shader, each shader uniform with its type, hint, range, default and the material's value, and why it cannot be drawn if so. Sky materials are read with assets.sky_material. |
| `assets.set_material` | `asset_set_material` | `path`: string (required)<br>`create`: boolean = `false`<br>`type`: string<br>`shader`: string | mutating | Create a surface or post-processing material, or change its shader. A surface material draws meshes whose renderer names it (scene.set_renderer material); a post-processing material is an effect in a Post Process node (scene.set_post_process). Parameters for uniforms the new shader lacks are kept but ignored. |
| `assets.set_material_parameter` | `asset_set_material_parameter` | `path`: string (required)<br>`name`: string (required)<br>`value`: number_array<br>`texture`: string<br>`reset`: boolean = `false` | mutating | Set one shader uniform on a material, saved to its file: value for numbers (1 to 4 numbers matching float, int, bool as 0 or 1, vec2, vec3 or vec4; colors are linear), or texture for sampler2D (a project PNG or JPEG, empty for the default image). reset returns the uniform to the shader's default. |
| `assets.sky_material` | `asset_sky_material` | `path`: string (required) | read-only | Read a sky material file (.relay-material) with its panorama image's size, or the reason the image cannot be drawn. |
| `assets.set_sky_material` | `asset_set_sky_material` | `path`: string (required)<br>`create`: boolean = `false`<br>`panorama`: string<br>`tint`: number_array<br>`intensity`: number<br>`rotationDegrees`: number | mutating | Create a sky material file (.relay-material), or change one. A sky material draws an equirectangular (2:1) panorama image from the project behind the scene, tinted, brightened and turned about the vertical axis; a sky uses it through scene.set_sky's material. Omitted fields keep their current values, or the defaults for a new file. |

Aggregates recent profiled frames into frame-time statistics, a CPU/GPU/display bottleneck verdict, a call tree of timed CPU scopes (simulation, scripts per behaviour, physics, rendering, editor UI and waits), hotspots by self time and per-pass GPU timings. Only a live editor records frames. |
| `profiler.set` | `profiler_set` | `paused`: boolean<br>`clear`: boolean = `false` | mutating | Pause the frame profiler to keep its recorded frames for inspection, or resume recording. Clearing discards recorded frames. |

Omitted settings keep their current values. Effects the GPU cannot run stay off and are reported by graphics.settings. |

| `scene.set_post_effect` | `scene_set_post_effect` | `entity`: string (required)<br>`index`: integer (required)<br>`enabled`: boolean<br>`editor`: boolean | mutating | Turn one post-processing effect on or off by its position in the list, without removing it, and choose whether it also shows in the editor's own view (off for effects meant for the game camera, such as motion blur). Undoable. |
| `scene.set_particle_emitter` | `scene_set_particle_emitter` | `entity`: string (required)<br>`attached`: boolean = `true`<br>`values`: object<br>`gesture`: integer | mutating | Add, edit or remove a node's particle emitter, for sparks, smoke, fire, dust, rain, magic, trails and explosions. values maps field names to JSON values: numbers, booleans, strings (choice names, a texture path, a sub emitter's child name), [x, y, z] vectors, [min, max] ranges picked at random per particle (or one number for both), [red, green, blue, alpha] sRGB colors from 0 to 1, curves as [[time, value], ...] and gradients as [[time, red, green, blue, alpha], ...] over each particle's life (time 0 at birth, 1 at death; no keys is 1 or white throughout), and bursts as [{"time", "count", "cycles", "interval", "probability"}]. The groups: emitter (play_on_start, looping, duration, prewarm, start_delay, max_particles, simulation_space world or local, simulation_speed, seed), emission (rate per second, rate_over_distance, bursts), shape (point, sphere, hemisphere, cone, box, circle or edge along +Y of the node, with radius, radius_thickness, angle, arc, box_size, shape_offset, shape_rotation, direction_randomness, spherize), particle (lifetime, speed, size, aspect, rotation, angular_velocity, color, and random_color with color_alt for a random mix per particle, inherit_velocity), motion (gravity as a multiple of 9.81 m/s², acceleration, velocity, drag, speed_over_lifetime, noise_strength, noise_frequency, noise_scroll), collision (none, plane at plane_height, or world colliders during Run Game, with bounce, friction, lifetime_loss, collision_radius), lifetime (size_over_lifetime, color_over_lifetime), sheet (flipbook columns, rows, mode, fps, cycles, random start, blend), renderer (texture or builtin_texture soft_dot, dot, ring, star, smoke, spark or square; blend alpha, additive or premultiplied; alignment billboard, stretched, horizontal, vertical or local; stretch_speed, stretch_length, emission brightness above 1 for glow, lit, soft_distance, sort) and sub_emitter (a child node's name, fired on death, collision or birth, with a count and inherited velocity). Omitted fields keep their values; a missing emitter is added with its defaults first. component.types lists every field with its type, range and choices. Undoable and saved with the scene; emitters preview in the editor, so check the look with a viewport capture. |
| `scene.set_ui` | `scene_set_ui` | `entity`: string (required)<br>`component`: string (required)<br>`attached`: boolean = `true`<br>`values`: object<br>`anchorPreset`: string<br>`presetMargin`: number = `0`<br>`gesture`: integer | mutating | Add, edit or remove one game interface (UI) component on a node. Interface nodes are drawn over the game's view during Run Game only, never in the editor's own view. A Canvas (ui_canvas) scales the controls below it to the screen; a Control (ui_control) places a rectangle, Godot style, by anchors (fractions of the parent control's or screen's size) plus offsets in canvas units, with a pivot for rotation and scale; widgets draw into it or react to the pointer: ui_panel, ui_label, ui_image, ui_button, ui_toggle (check box or switch), ui_slider, ui_progress_bar and ui_container (column, row or grid that places its children). values maps field names to JSON values: numbers, booleans, strings (text, project file paths, choice names), [x, y] vectors, [red, green, blue, alpha] sRGB colors from 0 to 1 and [left, top, right, bottom] margins. Omitted fields keep their values; a missing component is added with its defaults first, and a widget brings its Control. anchor_preset (ui_control) places the control by a preset before values apply, keeping its size. component.types lists every field with its type, range and choices; ui.layout and ui.render show the result. Undoable and saved with the scene. |
| `component.add` | `component_add` | `entity`: string (required)<br>`component`: string (required)<br>`behaviour`: string | mutating | Add an engine component with editor defaults, or append a script component running a behaviour, as one undoable transaction. Configure it afterwards with the component's own method, such as scene.set_camera or scene.set_script_property. |
| `component.remove` | `component_remove` | `entity`: string (required)<br>`component`: string (required)<br>`index`: integer | mutating, destructive | Remove one component as an undoable transaction. The Transform and imported model animation cannot be removed. |
| `component.set_enabled` | `component_set_enabled` | `entity`: string (required)<br>`component`: string (required)<br>`enabled`: boolean (required)<br>`index`: integer | mutating | Switch one component on or off without removing it or losing its settings, like the checkbox on a Unity component, as one undoable transaction. A disabled component stays on the node and in the scene file but does nothing: a disabled mesh renderer is not drawn, a disabled camera or sky is never the one in use, a disabled collider, physics body, joint, script, light, audio source, music player, reverb zone, particle emitter, keyframe animation or interface component is ignored during Run Game and in the editor view. The Transform and imported model animation cannot be disabled. |
| `scene.set_script` | `scene_set_script` | `entity`: string (required)<br>`index`: integer (required)<br>`behaviour`: string<br>`enabled`: boolean | mutating | Change the behaviour or enabled state of one of a node's script components, as an undoable transaction. |
| `scene.set_script_property` | `scene_set_script_property` | `entity`: string (required)<br>`index`: integer (required)<br>`property`: string (required)<br>`number`: number<br>`boolean`: boolean<br>`text`: string<br>`vector`: number_array<br>`reset`: boolean = `false`<br>`gesture`: integer | mutating | Store a value for a behaviour property on one script component, or reset it to the code default. Send exactly one of number, boolean, text or vector unless resetting. |

Bounds-level precision, not per-triangle. Stateless: the caller supplies the ray, so the engine stores no viewpoint. |

| `audio.status` | `audio_status` | — | read-only | Read the audio output device, the listener, every playing voice (clip, bus, position, gains) and each mixer bus with its post-fader peak and RMS levels in dB. |
| `audio.settings` | `audio_settings` | — | read-only | Read the project's mixer buses (settings.audio in the .relayproject): name, parent, volume in dB, mute and solo, with the defaults. |
| `audio.set_bus` | `audio_set_bus` | `name`: string (required)<br>`newName`: string<br>`parent`: string<br>`volumeDb`: number<br>`mute`: boolean<br>`solo`: boolean<br>`preview`: boolean = `false` | mutating | Create a bus, or change one's name, parent, volume, mute or solo, and save the mixer in the open project. A new bus defaults to Master as its parent. While any bus is soloed only soloed buses, their parents and their children are heard. Renaming keeps children attached; sources naming the old bus fall back to Master until they are changed. |
| `audio.remove_bus` | `audio_remove_bus` | `name`: string (required) | mutating, destructive | Remove a bus other than Master and save the mixer; its children move to its parent and sources routed to it play into Master. |
| `particles.status` | `particles_status` | `entity`: string | read-only | Report every particle emitter the simulation knows (or one): whether it is playing, paused, a sub emitter or finishing after its node went, how many particles are alive, and its time and cycle. In the editor every emitter previews; during Run Game emitters follow play_on_start, scripts and particles.control. |
| `particles.control` | `particles_control` | `entity`: string (required)<br>`action`: string (required)<br>`count`: integer = `10` | mutating | Play, restart, stop, clear, pause, resume or emit a burst from a node's particle emitter, in the editor preview or during Run Game. stop lets the living particles finish while clear removes them; emit adds count particles now from the emitter's shape. Not undoable: particles are not scene data. |
| `audio.play` | `audio_play` | `entity`: string (required) | mutating | Start or restart a node's audio source. During Run Game it plays as authored; in the editor it plays as a flat preview. |
| `audio.stop` | `audio_stop` | `entity`: string<br>`sound`: integer | mutating | Stop a node's audio source, a one-shot by the handle audio.play_clip returned, or every playing sound when neither is given. |
| `audio.clip` | `audio_clip` | `clip`: string (required)<br>`peaks`: integer = `0` | read-only | Decode a project sound file and report its duration, sample rate, channels and frames, with optional min/max peak pairs across it for drawing a waveform. |
| `audio.set_effect` | `audio_set_effect` | `bus`: string (required)<br>`index`: integer<br>`type`: string<br>`enabled`: boolean<br>`mix`: number<br>`roomSize`: number<br>`damping`: number<br>`width`: number<br>`preDelayMs`: number<br>`timeMs`: number<br>`feedback`: number<br>`lowDb`: number<br>`midDb`: number<br>`midFrequency`: number<br>`highDb`: number<br>`thresholdDb`: number<br>`ratio`: number<br>`attackMs`: number<br>`releaseMs`: number<br>`makeupDb`: number<br>`ceilingDb`: number<br>`cutoffHz`: number<br>`resonance`: number<br>`preview`: boolean = `false` | mutating | Add an effect to a mixer bus's chain (omit index), or change the effect at index, and save the mixer in the open project. Types and their parameters: reverb (room_size, damping, width, pre_delay_ms, mix), delay (time_ms, feedback, damping, mix), eq (low_db shelf at 200 Hz, mid_db at mid_frequency, high_db shelf at 5 kHz), compressor (threshold_db, ratio, attack_ms, release_ms, makeup_db), limiter (ceiling_db, release_ms), lowpass and highpass (cutoff_hz, resonance). Effects run in order before the bus volume; at most 8 per bus. |
| `audio.remove_effect` | `audio_remove_effect` | `bus`: string (required)<br>`index`: integer (required) | mutating, destructive | Remove the effect at index from a bus's chain and save the mixer. |
| `audio.move_effect` | `audio_move_effect` | `bus`: string (required)<br>`index`: integer (required)<br>`to`: integer (required) | mutating | Move the effect at index to position to in the same bus's chain and save the mixer. |
| `audio.debug_shapes` | `audio_debug_shapes` | — | read-only | Read reverb zones (centre, box edge vectors or sphere radius in world space, fade) and spatial sources (centre, minimum and maximum distance) for drawing them in a viewport. |
| `audio.music` | `audio_music` | `entity`: string (required)<br>`action`: string (required)<br>`track`: integer<br>`sync`: string<br>`fadeSeconds`: number = `1` | mutating | During Run Game: play a track (by playlist index), go to the next one, or stop with a fade. A change crossfades from the current track and lands on the next beat, bar or track end, or at once, as sync says (the player's own setting when omitted). |
| `audio.play_clip` | `audio_play_clip` | `clip`: string (required)<br>`x`: number<br>`y`: number<br>`z`: number<br>`volumeDb`: number = `0`<br>`pitch`: number = `1`<br>`bus`: string = `"SFX"`<br>`minDistance`: number = `1`<br>`maxDistance`: number = `50` | mutating | Play a project sound file once without a node: placed at x, y, z in the world during Run Game (flat in the editor, where it previews), or flat when no position is given. Returns a handle for audio.stop. |
| `audio.set_spatialization` | `audio_set_spatialization` | `mode`: string (required) | mutating | Set how positioned sounds reach the ears and save it in the open project: stereo panning for speakers, or binaural for headphones, where a head model gives each ear its own delay and shadow and sounds behind are slightly duller. |

## Generation

Edit `protocol/relay.protocol.json`, then run `python3 tools/generate_protocol.py`.
Use `python3 tools/generate_protocol.py --check` in CI to reject stale generated artifacts.
